reviewer: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), working for joshsu54
method: Each PNG opened and inspected visually in this session before any modelling; SHA-256 recomputed from the copied file and matched against the handoff SHA256SUMS.json and image-manifest.json.
priority_rule: user brief + AGENTS.md > README dimensions + image-manifest corrections > drawn silhouette/material > decoration. Perspective, dimension arrows and contradictory mechanics in the AI sheets are not copied.

shared_interface_decision.joint_rule: Every channel port end face is flat and carries a 10 mm deep x 21 mm wide U-groove following the bore at 40 mm offset. One separate JointGasket (clay-fibre, 20 mm wide, 20 mm thick installed / 23 mm free) sits half in each groove of a joint. Faces butt with 0 mm gap; the gasket is counted once per joint, never on both modules. Ports are direction-neutral (type channel_std), so a module may be placed reversed; flow direction is a property of the route, not of the module.
shared_interface_decision.why: The sheets draw a 20 mm gasket in a 20 mm recess on both mating faces; taken literally that double-counts the gasket or leaves a gap. Splitting the 20 mm recess as 10 + 10 keeps the drawn numbers and makes B03 usable for left and right turns by rotation.

assets.seen: Low square stone basin, 10 cm rim walls built from dressed blocks, raised corner caps, bronze vertical straps with bolts on each block joint. FRONT and BACK both show a centred open U port (corrected back view); RIGHT SIDE solid. Plan: interior 120 x 120, water flows back to front. Port detail and module joint drawn.
conflicts: Front/back ports drawn as waterfalls spilling over a lip; manifest says continuous floor at one height.
Water floor drawn 10 cm above ground; port floor also 10 cm -> consistent.
assets.decision: 140 x 140 x 0.40 m; basin floor top z=0.10 continuous with both port floors; 60 cm openings cut through front and back walls, no lip. Corner cap stones and bronze straps kept, corner caps sit inside the 1.40 footprint. Back port = inlet (spring side), front = outlet by route convention.

assets.seen: 1.0 m short trough: floor slab and two long wall slabs, end pilaster stones with bronze strap + timber key clamps on the outer faces at both ends. Both ends open (plan corrected). Joint section shows gasket between two flat faces.
conflicts: Pilasters drawn slightly taller/wider than the 60 x 40 profile.
assets.decision: Pilasters kept inside the 0.60 x 0.40 envelope (no step at the mating face); clamps are outside the walls only, 12 mm proud, do not cross the bore or the end plane.

assets.seen: L corner in a 100 x 100 footprint. Plan: inlet on the front (-Y) of the left leg, outlet on the right (+X) of the top leg, smooth inner fillet, outer corner square. Bronze clamps with ring ears on outer walls.
conflicts: Main views drawn with downward perspective; not usable for tracing.
assets.decision: Left leg x -0.50..0.10, top leg y -0.10..0.50; inlet centre (-0.20,-0.50), outlet centre (0.50,0.20). Inner bore turns on a 0.20 m centreline fillet; outer wall square. Left turns use the same mesh placed reversed (rotation only).

assets.seen: T junction, 120 x 100 footprint: front inlet stem 60 wide, cross channel to left (field) and right (branch), back wall closed, low chamfered splitter nose opposite the inlet. Timber+bronze bands on the back wall.
conflicts: Wall-thickness arrow drawn vertically (manifest: horizontal 10 cm).
Cross channel spans full 120 width so the side ports sit at x=+-0.60.
assets.decision: Stem y -0.50..-0.10 (centre x 0); cross channel y -0.10..0.50 with ports at x=+-0.60, centre y 0.20; back wall y 0.40..0.50 closed; splitter nose 8 cm high on the floor opposite the inlet. Exactly three ports.

assets.seen: Channel insert 30 cm deep with stone abutments, two cedar posts 150 cm, top beam, vertical toothed rack on the panel centre, bronze-cornered plank panel in side guides, side grips at 105 cm. OPEN state raised 32 cm. Detail shows pinion meshing the rack and the B06 shaft.
conflicts: Closed panel drawn with water visible under it (leak gap).
Pinion drawn in front of the rack while the shaft continues past it: the square coupling would hit the rack.
assets.decision: Closed panel bottom sits on the floor (z=0.10) in 22 mm deep wall slots. Rack teeth face +X; pinion sits beside the rack (axle along Y at x=+0.060, z=0.90) so the shaft passes beside the rack into front and rear bearing rails. Module 4 mm, 16-tooth pinion (pitch r 32 mm), rack pitch 12.57 mm. Rack length 0.85 passes through a slot in the top beam.
